sources.title: Filing text 0
sources.content: troubled debt restructurings ( tdrs ) a tdr is a loan whose terms have been restructured in a manner that grants a concession to a borrower experiencing financial difficulties .

sources.content: notes to consolidated financial statements derivatives with credit-related contingent features certain of the firm 2019s derivatives have been transacted under bilateral agreements with counterparties who may require the firm to post collateral or terminate the transactions based on changes in the firm 2019s credit ratings .

sources.title: Filing text 1
sources.content: the firm assesses the impact of these bilateral agreements by determining the collateral or termination payments that would occur assuming a downgrade by all rating agencies .

sources.title: Filing text 2
sources.content: a downgrade by any one rating agency , depending on the agency 2019s relative ratings of the firm at the time of the downgrade , may have an impact which is comparable to the impact of a downgrade by all rating agencies .

sources.title: Filing text 3
sources.content: the table below presents the aggregate fair value of net derivative liabilities under such agreements ( excluding application of collateral posted to reduce these liabilities ) , the related aggregate fair value of the assets posted as collateral , and the additional collateral or termination payments that could have been called at the reporting date by counterparties in the event of a one-notch and two-notch downgrade in the firm 2019s credit ratings. .

sources.title: Filing text 4
sources.content: additional collateral or termination payments for a one-notch downgrade 911 1534 additional collateral or termination payments for a two-notch downgrade 2989 2500 credit derivatives the firm enters into a broad array of credit derivatives in locations around the world to facilitate client transactions and to manage the credit risk associated with market- making and investing and lending activities .

sources.title: Filing text 5
sources.content: credit derivatives are actively managed based on the firm 2019s net risk position .

sources.title: Filing text 6
sources.content: credit derivatives are individually negotiated contracts and can have various settlement and payment conventions .

sources.title: Filing text 7
sources.content: credit events include failure to pay , bankruptcy , acceleration of indebtedness , restructuring , repudiation and dissolution of the reference entity .

sources.title: Filing text 8
sources.content: credit default swaps .

sources.title: Filing text 9
sources.content: single-name credit default swaps protect the buyer against the loss of principal on one or more bonds , loans or mortgages ( reference obligations ) in the event the issuer ( reference entity ) of the reference obligations suffers a credit event .

sources.title: Filing text 10
sources.content: the buyer of protection pays an initial or periodic premium to the seller and receives protection for the period of the contract .

sources.title: Filing text 11
sources.content: if there is no credit event , as defined in the contract , the seller of protection makes no payments to the buyer of protection .

sources.title: Filing text 12
sources.content: however , if a credit event occurs , the seller of protection is required to make a payment to the buyer of protection , which is calculated in accordance with the terms of the contract .

sources.title: Filing text 13
sources.content: credit indices , baskets and tranches .

sources.title: Filing text 14
sources.content: credit derivatives may reference a basket of single-name credit default swaps or a broad-based index .

sources.title: Filing text 15
sources.content: if a credit event occurs in one of the underlying reference obligations , the protection seller pays the protection buyer .

sources.title: Filing text 16
sources.content: the payment is typically a pro-rata portion of the transaction 2019s total notional amount based on the underlying defaulted reference obligation .

sources.title: Filing text 17
sources.content: in certain transactions , the credit risk of a basket or index is separated into various portions ( tranches ) , each having different levels of subordination .

sources.title: Filing text 18
sources.content: the most junior tranches cover initial defaults and once losses exceed the notional amount of these junior tranches , any excess loss is covered by the next most senior tranche in the capital structure .

sources.title: Filing text 19
sources.content: total return swaps .

sources.title: Filing text 20
sources.content: a total return swap transfers the risks relating to economic performance of a reference obligation from the protection buyer to the protection seller .

sources.title: Filing text 21
sources.content: typically , the protection buyer receives from the protection seller a floating rate of interest and protection against any reduction in fair value of the reference obligation , and in return the protection seller receives the cash flows associated with the reference obligation , plus any increase in the fair value of the reference obligation .

sources.title: Filing text 22
sources.content: credit options .

sources.title: Filing text 23
sources.content: in a credit option , the option writer assumes the obligation to purchase or sell a reference obligation at a specified price or credit spread .

sources.title: Filing text 24
sources.content: the option purchaser buys the right , but does not assume the obligation , to sell the reference obligation to , or purchase it from , the option writer .

sources.title: Filing text 25
sources.content: the payments on credit options depend either on a particular credit spread or the price of the reference obligation .

sources.content: goldman sachs 2013 annual report 147 .

sources.title: Filing text 4

sources.title: Filing text 5

sources.title: Filing text 6
sources.content: however , devon may elect to borrow at the prime rate .

sources.content: the senior credit facility contains only one material financial covenant .

sources.title: Filing text 4
sources.content: the maximum matching contribution for 2010 was pro-rated to account for the number of months remaining after the reinstatement .

sources.title: Filing text 5
sources.content: the company 2019s expenses for material defined contribution plans for the years ended december 31 , 2012 , 2011 and 2010 were $ 42 million , $ 48 million and $ 23 million , respectively .

sources.title: Filing text 6
sources.content: beginning january 1 , 2012 , the company may make an additional discretionary 401 ( k ) plan matching contribution to eligible employees .

sources.title: Filing text 7
sources.content: for the year ended december 31 , 2012 , the company made no discretionary matching contributions .

sources.title: Filing text 9
sources.content: share-based compensation plans and other incentive plans stock options , stock appreciation rights and employee stock purchase plan the company grants options to acquire shares of common stock to certain employees and to existing option holders of acquired companies in connection with the merging of option plans following an acquisition .

sources.title: Filing text 10
sources.content: each option granted and stock appreciation right has an exercise price of no less than 100% ( 100 % ) of the fair market value of the common stock on the date of the grant .

sources.title: Filing text 11

sources.title: Filing text 12
sources.content: stock options and stock appreciation rights assumed or replaced with comparable stock options or stock appreciation rights in conjunction with a change in control of the company only become exercisable if the holder is also involuntarily terminated ( for a reason other than cause ) or quits for good reason within 24 months of a change in control .

sources.title: Filing text 13
sources.content: the employee stock purchase plan allows eligible participants to purchase shares of the company 2019s common stock through payroll deductions of up to 20% ( 20 % ) of eligible compensation on an after-tax basis .

sources.title: Filing text 14
sources.content: plan participants cannot purchase more than $ 25000 of stock in any calendar year .

sources.title: Filing text 15
sources.content: the price an employee pays per share is 85% ( 85 % ) of the lower of the fair market value of the company 2019s stock on the close of the first trading day or last trading day of the purchase period .

sources.title: Filing text 16
sources.content: the plan has two purchase periods , the first one from october 1 through march 31 and the second one from april 1 through september 30 .

sources.title: Filing text 17
sources.content: for the years ended december 31 , 2012 , 2011 and 2010 , employees purchased 1.4 million , 2.2 million and 2.7 million shares , respectively , at purchase prices of $ 34.52 and $ 42.96 , $ 30.56 and $ 35.61 , and $ 41.79 and $ 42.00 , respectively .

sources.title: Filing text 18
sources.content: the company calculates the value of each employee stock option , estimated on the date of grant , using the black-scholes option pricing model .

sources.title: Filing text 20

sources.title: Filing text 21
sources.content: the selection of the implied volatility approach was based upon the availability of actively traded options on the company 2019s stock and the company 2019s assessment that implied volatility is more representative of future stock price trends than historical volatility .

sources.title: Filing text 22
sources.content: the risk-free interest rate assumption is based upon the average daily closing rates during the year for u.s .

sources.title: Filing text 23

sources.title: Filing text 24
